idea.value: A person gives a real tool three plain requests, and the film's own opening is the first result, so what you are watching is the proof.

audience.value: People who already use an AI assistant and edit video: named assistant models and an editor timeline are shown without explanation.

value.device: A plain claim typed in two parts while a person walks across the lens
value.description: The first line sits centred at about 17% of width; a passing body clears it letter by letter from 0.64 to 0.96 s. Silence at 1.17-1.75 s (measured) holds the gap, then the second half types on at 2.08-2.56 s. The ellipsis asks 'and?'.

value.purpose: Arrive at the product through the physical world
value.retentionDevice: Name on a prop, then a push into the screen
Text echo card, then a real folder collapse

value.purpose: Second request: edit, ending in recognition
value.retentionDevice: Quick human reactions, tightening pulse, own opening appears
value.content: Reaction, request, log, timeline, preview, monitor

value.retentionDevice: Stated doubt on black, then a shocked close-up that is itself generated material

payoff.value: The burst at 33.88-36.64 s, built from the product's own output, after the viewer has seen the requests that produced such material.

callToAction.value: An address only, on black, from 37.32 s, with no spoken or written request.

whyItWorks: Three requests in rising difficulty, each short enough to read: organise, edit, generate. Each is shown as typed text, then a real result.
Human reactions of 0.6-0.7 s separate the interface passages, so the viewer does not watch a screen for more than about 3.5 s without a person or a black card.
Real interface is cropped until one action fills the frame: fields at about 60% of width, not a window in a field.
Monitor push and pull-out make the software physically present.
Doubt is voiced by the film itself in plain words just before each proof.
